newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai seeks to become Gulf's industrial centre.
newsitem.headline: Dubai seeks to become Gulf's industrial centre.

text.p: United Arab Emirates member state Dubai, widely considered the Gulf's trading and tourism hub, is aiming to become the region's industrial centre.

A study outlining the strategy of a five-year development plan to the year 2000 said the scheme aimed for seven percent annual growth in the industrial sector, with special emphasis on petroleum products manufacturing.

"A wide variety of petrochemical industries based on primary raw materials, secondary products and derivatives would be viable and hence should be promoted for development," said the study by Dubai's Economic Department, received by Reuters on Monday.

It said petroleum products accounted for 19 percent of the emirate's total manufacturing output, but there was room for expansion through increased regional and international demand and Dubai's proximity to international markets.
To achieve industrial growth, the study proposed a 1,000 hectare (2,500 acre) industrial estate making lots available for investors on long-term leases for up to 60 years.
It said Dubai would encourage and take part in "investment zones" in what it termed investment growth triangles with Qatar, Iran, Oman, Pakistan and India.
"Dubai, being rich in capital and infrastructure, could participate in industrial ventures with sub-regions with large populations and markets as well as extensive resources," the study said.

The director-general of Dubai's Economic Department, Mohammad Alabbar, said earlier that the emirate hoped to attract investment of 44.5 billion dirhams ($12.13 billion) to the year 2000, with about 12 billion dirhams going to the manufacturing sector.

Dubai, which pumps some 300,000 barrels of oil per day, aims for five percent annual GDP growth and a yearly 6.9 percent increase in non-oil GDP up to 2000. It also seeks to raise the non-oil sector's contribution to GDP to 88.7 percent.
